subject: Output Entitlement & Training Opt-out — evidence list and ops runbook
messages:
From: Evan Turner <evan.turner@brightbox.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@brightbox.ai
Date: 2026-10-20 09:15 -0700
Subject: Questions on 'Output Ownership' & training opt-out language (MSA redlines)

Hi Mateo,

Quick follow-up from our legal team after reviewing the MSA + Order Form you sent. There are two principal asks they flagged that will block procurement on our side:

1) Output ownership: the redline currently assigns rights to Redwood for "processed output" derived from Customer Content. We need narrow, customer-first language that preserves Brightbox ownership of any customer-generated output used in their product unless explicitly licensed back to Redwood for model ops.

2) Training/feedback: legal wants a clear opt-out path (order-form level) plus a list of operational evidence proving you do not use Brightbox data for model training when opted-out (audit logs, KV cache segregation, S3 object retention windows, KMS key IDs, and a timeline for retention).

I've attached our annotated redline (Brightbox_MSA_redline_v3.pdf). Can you send a proposed wording and the operational evidence checklist you can commit to? Procurement is targeting sign by 11/05, so timelines are tight.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Turner
Head of Legal Ops
Brightbox Analytics

-- attachment: Brightbox_MSA_redline_v3.pdf (PDF, 612KB)

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Evan Turner <evan.turner@brightbox.ai>

Subject: Re: Questions on 'Output Ownership' & training opt-out language (MSA redlines)

Evan — thanks for the clear summary and for the redline. Appreciate the timeline callout.

High-level: we can accept a narrowly defined customer ownership carveout for productized customer outputs and provide an opt-out at the Order Form level for training/feedback. To get this over the finish line we need to: (a) propose substitute contract text, and (b) provide a short ops evidence checklist that we can commit to operationally and include as an appendix to the order form.

I'm looping in Marissa (legal), Laura (procurement lead for the account), and Karthik (sales) to help. Action plan:
- Marissa and I will draft substitute MSA/Order Form language today and circulate.
- Laura and our ops team will produce the evidence checklist and retention windows (ETA 10/22).
- Karthik will confirm commercial implications of the opt-out (credits/pricing) and share a proposed amendment if needed.

We'll aim to send a consolidated response with attached drafts by EOD 10/21. Does that work for you?

Thanks,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

-- inline: Proposed turnaround and owners

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-20 13:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on 'Output Ownership' & training opt-out language (MSA redlines)

Attn team — drafting notes below (I kept the language intentionally narrow to preserve productization flexibility while addressing their ask):

- Output: propose language replacing the "Redwood owns processed output" clause with: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Content and in Output that is the direct result of Customer Content as used solely within Customer's product. Redwood's use of such Output is limited to providing the Services and supporting the Agreement, except where Customer grants a separate license."

- Training opt-out: two-tier approach — (1) Order Form flag to opt-out of "Feedback & Training" (checkbox) and (2) a short Ops Appendix listing the technical controls Redwood will apply when opt-out is selected. The Appendix items should be operationally verifiable (see checklist below).

Suggested Ops Appendix checklist (what we can commit to):
1) Request-level metadata tagging and retention policy (logs retained X days).
2) KV cache isolation per-customer for opted-out customers; no persistent checkpoint snapshots used for model training.
3) Audit logs showing inference requests and model variant used (exportable CSV).
4) Object retention policy for customer uploads (S3 TTL in days).
5) KMS key rotation schedule and ability to identify customer-associated key IDs.
6) SOC2 + encryption-at-rest summary and link to current attestation (if available under NDA).

I flagged items 1, 2 and 3 as the minimum Brightbox will ask for. Laura: please own producing an Excel checklist and marking what we can provide via portal vs NDA/secure transfer. Karthik: we should propose a small recurring credit for customers who opt-out to reflect reduced productization value — draft a banded credit proposal.

I'll draft the redline text and attach a response doc for Evan to track.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Evan Turner <evan.turner@brightbox.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-21 09:05 -0700
Subject: Attached: response draft + ops evidence checklist (see summary)

Evan — attaching our draft response and the ops evidence checklist for the opt-out flow. Summary of the key points below and proposed redline excerpts are in redline-response-draft.docx. Link to the ops runbook is included for your security team review.

Summary (short):
- Output: we will accept a customer-output carveout narrowly scoped to "Output that directly results from Customer Content and is consumed by Customer's product". Redwood retains the right to use aggregated telemetry for service improvement but not to claim ownership of customer outputs.
- Opt-out: single checkbox on the Order Form to opt-out of Feedback & Training; selecting opt-out triggers the Ops Appendix controls below.

Ops Appendix (what we'll commit to operationally if opt-out selected):
- KV cache segregation for opt-out customers; no material logging of prompt/response bodies to training pipelines.
- Request-level audit exports (CSV) showing request timestamps, model variant, latency, and a hash of input ID; retention: 90 days by default, configurable to 30 days on request.
- Clear S3 retention TTLs for customer uploads; by default 30 days for ephemeral artifacts, 365 days for backups (can be shortened on request).
- Provide KMS key IDs used for customer data encryption; support for customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments.
- SOC2 summary and ability to share SOC2 report under NDA.

Attachments: redline-response-draft.docx, ops-evidence-checklist.xlsx

Can you confirm the above addresses Brightbox's asks and whether legal needs the SOC2 under NDA or an inventory of specific artifacts? If you confirm, we'll finalize the MSA redline and send a counter-order form for signature.

Best,
Mateo

-- attachments: redline-response-draft.docx (Word, 24KB); ops-evidence-checklist.xlsx (Excel, 18KB)

From: Evan Turner <evan.turner@brightbox.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@brightbox.ai
Date: 2026-10-21 11:47 -0700
Subject: Re: Attached: response draft + ops evidence checklist (see summary)

Mateo — that summary gets us most of the way there, thank you. A couple clarifications from legal: 

1) The "aggregated telemetry" carve-out: we need a line clarifying that aggregation excludes any direct use of Customer Content or Output for model training or fine-tuning without explicit, separate written consent.
2) Retention windows: legal would prefer default request-log retention of 30 days and a firm commitment that customer can request a shorter retention period in writing. If certain artifacts must be retained longer for telemetry/debugin, we need to list them and provide justification.
3) SOC2: legal will accept SOC2 summary first, and will request the full report under NDA if required during final diligence.

Procurement would also like to see a DocuSign-ready version of the counter-order form with the opt-out checkbox and the Ops Appendix attached so they can sign internal approvals. Can you circulate that by EOD 10/22?

Thanks,
Evan
